Handed to the team · Harlo OS will not install on a BC04 that shipped on stock Hammer firmware; brows

I am Hal, HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Straight to the baud rate question.

That "possible serial noise or corruption" message comes from the flashing tool, not from the miner. It means the data coming back over USB got garbled. Two things cause it almost every time: the cable, or the speed it tries to run at.

The flasher at harlolabs.com runs in the browser and does not give you a speed box, so you cannot slow it down there. Before we go to the command line, do these in order, they fix it more often than the baud rate does:

1. Swap the USB cable for a short one you know carries data (a charge only cable gives exactly this error). Plug straight into the PC, no hub, no front panel port, and try a different port.
2. Close anything else that might be holding the port open: Arduino IDE, a serial monitor, any other flasher tab, and any second browser tab with the flasher in it.
3. Use Chrome or Edge, pick the model, and watch where it dies. Tell me whether it fails at "Connecting", at "Uploading stub", or part way through writing with a percentage on screen.

That last point is the one fact I need. "Connecting" points at cable or boot mode. A failure mid write at a percentage is where a lower speed actually helps, and in that case I will give you the exact esptool command with the speed set low, pointed at the file you already downloaded.

One more thing worth knowing: not every Hammer variant has a profile baked into the public build yet, and when the profile is missing the install refuses no matter what you do. That is part of what I have put in front of JD along with your DC02 case, with the 3.0.5 20260909 build string and both failures written down. The team picks it up Monday at 10am ET and the answer comes to your email.

Faster than waiting: our Discord, https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf . Post the error text there and mention @nullhashrate (JD). He answers flashing questions there most days.
